key_insight: Retired DDR4 is wafer-free capacity; a CXL tier for cold pages or KV spill monetizes it at roughly 10-20% of new-DDR5 cost per GB.
killer_doubt: Already shipping: Marvell Structera X reuses DDR4 and Microsoft GreenSKU did it. The pool is one-time (DDR4 is EOL), and CXL adds ~70-100 ns over local DRAM.
decisive_experiment: Size the supply: burn-in a few thousand decommissioned RDIMMs to get the fallout rate, plus a survey of retirement volume. If it is under ~1% of annual DRAM bits, it stays a niche.
prior_art: Marvell Structera X (DDR4-reuse CXL controller), Microsoft GreenSKU (ISCA 2024), Azure Pond / Meta CXL pooling studies.

key_insight: Draw-stack-redraw (microchannel-plate style) makes high-AR Cu via fields in one thermal process; a dense random via field needs no registration, like an anisotropic conductor.
killer_doubt: Via density is not the memory bottleneck (lateral RDL is). Cu-glass CTE mismatch (~1.3% strain over ~1000 K) debonds cores; molten-Cu cores under 5 um risk Rayleigh breakup.
decisive_experiment: At a university fiber tower, draw and redraw a Cu-in-borosilicate rod and slice 100 um discs. Map via continuity, resistance and hermeticity after 1000 cycles of -55/125 C. About $150k.
prior_art: Taylor-Ulitovsky Cu microwire; microchannel-plate and fiber-faceplate draw-stack-redraw; LPKF LIDE laser TGVs; Intel/Absolics glass-core substrates.

key_insight: Edge I/O on face-to-back die blocks removes TSVs and the interposer, so each die keeps DDR-class density while a 32-die block over a GPU gives ~100 GB at HBM-class width.
killer_doubt: Edge pads fit only the ~5-10 um BEOL band: ~25k contacts per die, not 250k. Diced cross-sections need <1 nm roughness to bond. Mm-long on-die paths give ~1 pJ/bit.
decisive_experiment: Bond 8 thinned dummy dies face-to-back into a block, CMP one edge to expose BEOL lines, and hybrid-bond it to a test wafer at 5 um pitch. Measure daisy-chain yield and shear after thermal cycling. About $400k.
prior_art: Irvine Sensors edge-metallized memory cubes, Vertical Circuits/Invensas sidewall-interconnect stacks, 3D-Plus; SK hynix VFO vertical wires. No 2 um edge hybrid bonding found.

key_insight: Rotating vectors before integer quantization bounds worst-case bit-flip damage and flattens outliers, so AI tensors degrade gracefully instead of catastrophically, as FP16 exponent flips do.
killer_doubt: Orthonormal transforms preserve error energy. At 1% BER a 128-d int8 vector takes ~10 flips (SNR ~6 dB). At a realistic 1e-4 BER, dropping ECC saves only ~12% capacity.
decisive_experiment: Software fault injection into FAISS, DLRM and KV tensors, with and without Hadamard spreading, at BER 1e-5 to 1e-2. Measure recall@10 and perplexity. About a week of GPU time, under $20k.
prior_art: EDEN (MICRO 2019) error-tolerant DNNs on approximate DRAM; QuaRot, QuIP# and SpinQuant Hadamard rotations; Flikker critical-data partitioning.

key_insight: HBM stack-ID addressing lets the base die fuse out a failed die group, so 12-high fallout can be salvaged as 8-high or half-width capacity bins.
killer_doubt: Most HBM loss is TSV and bond failure; known-good-die screening already removes bad dies. Salvage adds perhaps 5-10% supply, within existing vendor binning. Outsiders cannot access fallout.
decisive_experiment: Using one vendor's fallout data, classify 1,000 failed stacks by failure locus: single die, TSV/bond or base die. A salvageable share above ~30% would justify a fuse-map rebin flow.
prior_art: Vendor speed and capacity binning plus lane repair; NVIDIA H100 PCIe ships 5 of 6 stacks enabled; partial-good salvage is standard in logic.

key_insight: Block summary keys in HBM, with full KV in CXL or flash, cut the HBM KV footprint 4-8x at small accuracy cost.
killer_doubt: Already published as Quest page min/max keys, InfLLM block representatives and ShadowKV landmarks with KV on the CPU. Fetches from CXL/flash (~1-100 us) stall decode unless prefetched.
decisive_experiment: Nothing new to settle. Reproduce ShadowKV/Quest on RULER-128k with KV on CXL versus HBM to measure the residual HBM fraction and tokens/s.
prior_art: Quest (ICML 2024), InfLLM (2024), ShadowKV (2024), InfiniGen (OSDI 2024), RetrievalAttention, PQCache.

key_insight: Scoring 4-bit key sketches at bank bandwidth (LPDDR5X-PIM is 8x internal) and returning only top-k indices lets long-context KV live in commodity PIM DRAM instead of HBM (~3x wafer/bit).
killer_doubt: DRAM-process logic is costly: Samsung HBM-PIM dies held half the bits (4 vs 8 Gb). Top-k must cost under ~10% die area and hold RULER accuracy at k~1-2%.
decisive_experiment: Run sketch scoring plus top-k on UPMEM PIM DIMMs or Ramulator2+DRAMPower. Synthesize a per-bank top-k unit at 28 nm, scaled to 3-metal DRAM. Measure tokens/s, pJ/token and RULER-128k accuracy. About $250k.
prior_art: SK hynix GDDR6-AiM and Samsung HBM-PIM/LPDDR5X-PIM (dense GEMV); IBM StarC selective token access on PIM; H2EAL hybrid-bonded top-k (via search snippet).

key_insight: HBM4 custom logic base dies make in-stack top-k deployable without touching DRAM arrays; only indices and selected values cross the PHY.
killer_doubt: The base die sees only TSV bandwidth, about equal to the ~2 TB/s PHY, so decode gets no speedup. The gain is PHY/interposer energy, ~20-30% of 3-4 pJ/bit.
decisive_experiment: Model base-die internal versus PHY bandwidth from HBM4 TSV and channel specs. If internal is at least 2x PHY, synthesize the scorer at N12/N5 in 3-5% of base-die area and simulate decode tokens/s. Under $100k.
prior_art: AttAcc (ASPLOS 2024) attention on HBM-PIM; Duplex (MICRO 2024) logic-die PIM; HBM4 custom base dies (SK hynix/TSMC, Samsung).

key_insight: An idle session needs only its 2-byte tokens. Re-prefilling on resume trades FLOPs for bytes and frees resident KV in proportion to the idle duty cycle.
killer_doubt: vLLM already offers recompute preemption. Re-prefilling 100k tokens costs seconds of accelerator time, which is why CachedAttention and LMCache spill KV to DRAM or SSD. Old-node chiplets worsen FLOPs/W.
decisive_experiment: Trace-driven simulation on public multi-turn chat timings: DRAM-GB saved versus added GPU-seconds for recompute, compared with SSD spill. Under $20k.
prior_art: vLLM recompute preemption; CachedAttention (ATC 2024); HCache (EuroSys 2025) hidden-state restore; Mooncake and LMCache KV tiers.

key_insight: Shared system prompts make KV highly redundant across users; content-addressed blocks store each shared prefix once.
killer_doubt: Host software already deduplicates exactly (vLLM automatic prefix caching, SGLang RadixAttention) with no hashing hardware. Base-die hashing adds latency and recovers nothing the scheduler misses.
decisive_experiment: Measure the duplicate 4 KB blocks left in HBM after RadixAttention on an agent-heavy trace. If under 10%, hardware dedup is moot. Software only, under $10k.
prior_art: vLLM automatic prefix caching; SGLang RadixAttention; hardware-deduplicated memory (HICAMP, ASPLOS 2012).

key_insight: CDS dynamically cancels receiver offset and 1/f drift, allowing ~30 mV swings. It is better aimed at DRAM's on-die global data lines, the dominant HBM energy term.
killer_doubt: The PHY is only ~0.5-1 of HBM's 3-4 pJ/bit, and ground-referenced or capacitive low-swing links already reach ~0.3-0.5 pJ/b. The reset phase halves per-lane throughput.
decisive_experiment: 28 nm MPW: a 1 mm interposer-class line with a CDS receiver at 30 mV versus a calibrated StrongARM baseline. Measure extrapolated BER and fJ/bit at 4-8 Gb/s across temperature. About $150k.
prior_art: NVIDIA ground-referenced signaling (2013); capacitively driven low-swing interconnects (Ho, Horowitz); offset-calibrated sense amplifiers; double-sampling comparators.

key_insight: Frozen weights need zero write endurance, so they can leave DRAM for surplus mature-node mask ROM. A 3-8B on-device model in ROM frees ~4-8 GB of LPDDR per AI phone.
killer_doubt: Model churn: phones live ~4 years while base models change yearly. And 28 nm NAND-ROM (~0.005 um2/bit) is ~2x DRAM area per bit, so expect cost parity, not 5x cheaper.
decisive_experiment: 40/28 nm MPW: a 16-64 Mb via-programmed NAND-ROM macro holding a quantized model slice, measuring density, read pJ/bit and page bandwidth. Add an accuracy study of LoRA on a ROM base across model generations. About $400k.
prior_art: Taalas HC1 (N6, weights in mask-ROM metal/via layers; AMD acquiring) (via search snippet); Hidden-ROM and YOLoC ROM-CiM (2022); SanDisk/SK hynix HBF.
